title: ArborBank POC streaming handshake tune sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on reducing TTFT variance caused by streaming handshake and intermittent kernel fallback. Reviewed latest benchmark runs (sequence 256/512), discussed root cause hypothesis for sporadic 1st-token spikes, agreed on kernel pinning and a short profiling run. Security asks noted around audit logs and KMS for Dedicated pilot.

ArborBank to share production token length histogram for customer traffic by 2026-03-25

Schedule optional deep-dive on KMS/HSM with security team 2026-03-29

Sofia Martinez: export and share real token length histogram for 30k requests — due 2026-03-25

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood Infra), Sofia Martinez (ArborBank), David Huang (ArborBank), Karen O'Neill (ArborBank Security), Mike Park (ArborBank Product)

Summary (auto): weekly POC check-in, focus on TTFT variance and streaming handshake.

[00:00] Alex Chen: ok good morning everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight 45 minute ish, main goal is to validate whether the handshake/retry behavior in streaming is producing the TTFT spikes you saw last week.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: yeah thanks alex, we saw, um, a bunch of first token outliers, like 200ms median but spikes to 1.2s on some, we flagged it in the dashboard, we can share the grafana dash.
[00:31] David Huang: and to add, those spikes happen seemingly at low concurrency, so it's not just a queuing issue, that's what puzzled us.
[00:45] Priya Kapoor: right that's helpful — our working hypothesis is either kernel fallback or intermittent network handshake retry on the streaming path, sometimes the runtime falls back to a generic attention kernel which adds 700ms for the first token.
[01:02] Karen O'Neill: security note before we dive too deep — if you pull traces can you redact PII automatically? we need to know what logs Redwood will share for the Dedicated pilot.
[01:15] Alex Chen: yep we can annotate and redact traces, for Dedicated we integrate with your KMS, and we can limit the retention window — we'll include that in the security checklist.
[01:25] Mike Park: also timeline note — execs want to see clear TTFT improvement within two weeks to commit to Dedicated.

[03:12] Priya Kapoor: ok going through the run we did Monday, we profiled 10k streamed calls at seq len 256 and 512, distribution was synthetic 60/40 256/512, but we also did a mixed run. There were 24 spikes >900ms. We correlated kernel logs and 18 of those had a kernel switch event within 200ms before the response.
[03:39] Sofia Martinez: when you say kernel switch, is that the runtime choosing a different GEMM or like a quantized path?
[03:47] Priya Kapoor: yeah it's the fallback to the generic aten-like kernel due to shape mismatch — sometimes the compiled fast-path wasn't chosen. It's subtle; on Ampere sometimes the kernel selector misclassifies under certain batch/seq combos.
[04:02] Marcus Lee: to add, we've seen the kernel selector use a safety path when memory pressure is detected, could be KV cache size or small transient memory noise.
[04:15] David Huang: are you seeing any correlation with background GC or other processes? our infra team uses ephemeral sidecars which might spike memory.
[04:28] Priya Kapoor: we didn't see GC in the runtime logs, but we did see network retransmits for a subset — that's why we suspect a compounded issue: a slight network retry plus kernel fallback equals a big spike.

[06:05] Alex Chen: ok hypothesis confirmed-ish: two factors. next I want to go through an action plan: 1) kernel pinning on pilot nodes for the next run, 2) forced handshake path that avoids re-negotiation once session is warm, 3) capture full-stream traces including socket RTTs, and 4) customer to provide token length histogram to adjust sequence bins.
[06:33] Sofia Martinez: quick question — kernel pinning means we force the fast path even if it was a shape mismatch? is there a stability risk?
[06:41] Priya Kapoor: pinning forces selection of the preferred kernel for the model + typical seq lengths; if shapes are within expected ranges it's safe. If we see out of distribution shapes, we put a guard to fall back, but initial run will be conservative.
[06:56] Karen O'Neill: and during pinning, will we still get audit logs for kernel selection? we need that for our compliance team.
[07:03] Marcus Lee: yes we log kernel decisions and can stream them to your SIEM; we can also increase retention for the POC.

[09:20] David Huang: on the networking side we captured some SYN retransmits at 100-200ms intervals around the spikes, possibly due to wacky egress routing. we'll overlay those traces.
[09:33] Priya Kapoor: great if you can share the PCAP or the TCP metrics that helps, otherwise we'll capture socket RTTs on our side.
[09:40] Sofia Martinez: we'll anonymize and share by tomorrow.

[11:01] Priya Kapoor: for the bench we'll run two modes: A) kernel-pinned + streaming handshake warm path, B) baseline with no pinning. each will run 6 hours with production-like concurrency (1-5 qps per worker), we'll collect first-byte histograms, kernel logs, and tcp socket stats.
[11:20] Alex Chen: schedule wise Priya will kick it off Tuesday night (that's 2026-03-23 03:00 UTC?), results and raw traces by Wednesday morning your time.
[11:32] Priya Kapoor: yep I'll run the bench and share a drive link to raw traces + a short summary. note: the traces are large, expect a ~3GB bucket for the 6-hour run.

[13:50] Mike Park: shifting to sequence length distribution — we've been using synthetic 60/40 but in production 90% of messages are short (<=64 tokens) with the occasional long session. that could change kernel decisioning.
[14:05] Priya Kapoor: that matters — fast-path kernels often assume short seq; we will run an additional <64 token bin to validate.
[14:15] Sofia Martinez: we'll export the histogram for 30k requests and send it.

[16:40] Karen O'Neill: security deep-dive: for Dedicated pilot we need KMS integration (HSM preferred), SOC2 report, ability to rotate keys, and immutable audit logs for kernel selection and request metadata. also can Redwood redact traces automatically?
[16:58] Alex Chen: we support KMS + HSM integration; for the pilot we'll provide a security checklist doc, SOC2 report, and an export that redacts PII. automatic redaction is a feature of our trace exporter, we'll include instructions.
[17:15] Karen O'Neill: also need proof that kernel logs do not leak prompt text — we just need metadata (kernel name, decision time, flags).
[17:25] Priya Kapoor: agreed; logs contain only model metadata, shape, and timestamps — no prompt payload.

[19:10] David Huang: question on autoscale burst — earlier we saw microbursts of traffic trigger new pods and that temporarily increased latency. can Redwood pre-warm or keep a small warm pool?
[19:24] Marcus Lee: Dedicated supports reserved warm slots and a small keep-alive pool; we can also configure pre-warming policy tied to a traffic schedule.
[19:35] Sofia Martinez: for cost reasons we'd prefer minimal warm pool but want to avoid spikes. what's the tradeoff?
[19:41] Alex Chen: small warm pool buys you better TTFT for rarely-bursting patterns, cost is linear with reserved capacity. we can simulate cost delta and show you an ROI for different warm sizes.

[22:00] Priya Kapoor: ok back to bench specifics — we'll instrument to tag every streaming session with handshake version and kernel id, plus socket RTT. that'll let us correlate spikes to network vs kernel.
[22:14] Sofia Martinez: will you also capture GC and memory pressure events?
[22:20] Priya Kapoor: yes we'll enable memory hooks and runtime GC markers.

[24:01] Alex Chen: let's talk acceptance criteria — what does success look like for ArborBank?
[24:09] Sofia Martinez: reduce 95th TTFT from ~900-1200ms down to <350ms for short messages and keep variance under 150ms.
[24:18] Mike Park: and confirm no PII leaks in traces, KMS integration review passed by security.
[24:25] Karen O'Neill: also need SLA target for Dedicated pilot: 99.9% p95 TTFT and audit logs turned on.

[26:40] Priya Kapoor: noted. we'll aim to show a p95 improvement in the pinned run. if we still see spikes we'll run a deeper kernel engineering pass and possibly recompile an explicit fast-path for your token shape.
[27:00] David Huang: how long would a kernel recompile take? we have change windows.
[27:06] Marcus Lee: minor recompile and validation is about 2-3 business days, full validation on multiple hardware ~1 week.

[29:30] Alex Chen: ok next steps recap: Priya runs the 6-hour pinned vs baseline bench and shares traces; Sofia shares token histograms; Marcus adds egress metrics; Alex sends pricing and security checklist; schedule security deep-dive.
[29:52] Sofia Martinez: confirmed.
[30:00] Priya Kapoor: will also attach a short runbook for how kernel pinning is toggled so you can understand the safety guards.

[32:10] Mike Park: one more ask — can you provide a short spreadsheet showing cost delta between keeping 2 vs 5 warm slots for 99k monthly calls? we'll need that to justify risk.
[32:21] Alex Chen: yes I can put together cost delta table by tomorrow.

[34:45] Karen O'Neill: any blockers from security? not yet, we'll review the checklist once you send it.
[34:53] Alex Chen: great, I'll include SOC2, key rotation docs, and redaction flow.

[36:02] David Huang: small transcription glitch earlier — sometimes the session label appears as Speaker 2 in our capture, sorry if that messes with your trace tags.
[36:12] Priya Kapoor: we can map session ids back to real runs if you include the mapping file.

[40:00] Alex Chen: ok wrapping — thanks everyone. to confirm deadlines: Priya 2026-03-24 traces, Sofia 2026-03-25 histogram, Alex pricing 2026-03-26, security deep-dive 2026-03-29.
[40:20] Sofia Martinez: sounds good.
[40:30] Karen O'Neill: thanks all.

[47:55] Alex Chen: thanks team, we'll follow up via email and shared drive, end call.
questions: What is the exact token length distribution for 30k customer requests?
Can Redwood redact PII from raw traces automatically?
What is the expected time to recompile an optimized kernel for our seq shapes?
